content.text: The migrated code compiles, but it still carries dpct headers and `dpct::` calls, and its launch uses `reqd_sub_group_size(32)` and 3-D indexing. I'll rewrite it as a 1-D port with two kernels: one work-item per slice, and one work-group per slice using group reductions. That works for any sub-group size, and it uses `sycl::exp` rather than `native::exp` so the results stay within 1e-6 of `expf`.

input.summary: Ported softmax.cu to SYCL 2020 in softmax_sycl.cpp (compiles with icpx -fsycl, add_dpct_include=false, no dpct headers, no dpct:: helpers or DPCT macros). Two 1-D kernels: kernel 0 is one work-item per slice; kernel 1 is one work-group (256 items) per slice using sycl::reduce_over_group for max and sum, so it does not depend on sub-group size and needs no reqd_sub_group_size or warp-32 assumptions. Uses sycl::exp (not native::exp) to stay close to expf. Verified against a host expf reference (check.cpp): max abs error 1.0e-7 (kernel 1, 8192x256), 1.9e-9 (kernel 0), 6.7e-8 (1000x100), 1.9e-9 (777x300), 0 (5x1), all within atol 1e-6. Caveat: the CUDA original was not built or run here, so the reference is the original formula computed on the host, not the CUDA binary output. The migrated/ directory from c2s is left as-is and is not the deliverable.
